ageing_relevance.rationale: TIMP1 is a GrimAge plasma-protein surrogate and has a sizeable ageing literature share, with weak-to-moderate associations with several age-related diseases. The GrimAge surrogate is a methylation estimate, not a measured protein level, and it showed no significant difference in the schizophrenia meta-analysis main model.

evidence.value: One of seven plasma proteins whose DNA-methylation surrogates make up GrimAge, the mortality clock that was +4.3 years older in schizophrenia in part 1 of this project (an effect explained by smoking). The surrogates are methylation estimates, not measured protein levels. Not significantly different in the main model of Shirai et al. 2024's meta-analysis.

background_knowledge: Circulating TIMP1 rises with age and predicts mortality and cardiovascular risk in epidemiological studies.

mechanism.rationale: TIMP1 has a well-defined biochemistry as an MMP inhibitor and also acts as a signalling growth factor. Its causal role in ageing is unclear: it may be a marker of tissue remodelling or inflammation, or it may be protective, so the direction of modulation is not obvious.

evidence.value: Metalloproteinase inhibitor that functions by forming one to one complexes with target metalloproteinases, such as collagenases, and irreversibly inactivates them by binding to their catalytic zinc cofactor.
Also functions as a growth factor that regulates cell differentiation, migration and cell death and activates cellular signaling cascades via CD63 and ITGB1.

background_knowledge: Higher TIMP1 may reflect fibrosis and inflammation, but whether it drives or protects against ageing phenotypes is not settled.

tractability.rationale: Open Targets lists no small-molecule or other-modality tractability. It lists only antibody-class (secreted, extracellular) and PROTAC database-ubiquitination flags. TIMP1 is a secreted protein with a pleiotropic function, so drugging it is difficult.

safety.rationale: Open Targets lists two generic liabilities (gene expression and transcription factor regulation), which carry little specific information. TIMP1 broadly regulates MMP activity and extracellular matrix remodelling, so modulating it risks effects on tissue remodelling and on cancer. Data are limited, so I did not score higher.
background_knowledge: MMP inhibitors as a class caused musculoskeletal toxicity in clinical trials.
TIMP1 is implicated in tumour biology.

clinical_precedence.rationale: No drugs acting on TIMP1 are listed.
